Lab reference · Tanium Cloud · September 2026

How a patch run moves through the chain

One Automate playbook drives four packages on danubu01. Every step is gated on what the endpoint reports, not on what the script says. This is the path a single run takes, from payload to applied.

Verified means the state changedPackage verification is a sensor query, so a script that exits 0 with the wrong state still fails verification. Exit code and verification are separate claims.
Gates never trust the consolerequire_state in every script refuses out-of-order runs with exit 90 and leaves the state alone. A targeting mistake shows as a code, not as a corrupted endpoint.
Rollback is a decision, not a reflexA conflict (73) leaves nothing to roll back; a failed apply does. Keeping rollback outside the chain means a person or a second playbook chooses.

What was built, and why each part is there

There is no Solaris or Oracle in the lab. The orchestration layer only ever sees a command line, an exit code and an inventory, so those three things are faked on an Ubuntu VM and everything on the Tanium side is real.

Decisions taken on the way

DecisionReason
Scripts hosted as release assets, not raw GitHubTanium Cloud cached the release zip in seconds but left every raw.githubusercontent.com file at 0 bytes. Same repo, same bytes, so it is egress filtering on the Tanium side. Release download URLs are on the same host as the payload, so one allow-list entry covers all of it.
Sensor name carries the EPX prefixConsole naming convention. Every gate and verification query therefore reads EPX - Oracle Patch State:State equals …. No underscore in the name, because Tanium uses _ as the sub-column separator in parameterised packages.
Verification by sensor query, not exit codeAn out-of-order Apply exits 90 and sits at Pending verification until the expiry, then Verification failed. That is the right answer: the endpoint never reached applied. Exit-code verification would have called the same run a success.
require_state leaves the state file aloneA step arriving out of sequence is a targeting mistake, not a patch failure. Recording it as failed would hide what the endpoint is actually in and could trigger a rollback of nothing.
Playbook has no rollback stepAutomate chains are linear. A conflict (73) needs a DBA, not a rollback; a failed apply needs a rollback now. Keeping 4 Rollback outside the chain makes that a choice, taken against State equals failed.
Step duration 25 minutes on Deploy stepsAutomate sets the floor from the package's command plus download timeout (10 + 15). The step ends as soon as every targeted endpoint completes, so in practice it is seconds. For a real OPatch apply the command timeout goes to 60 minutes and the floor follows.
Packages in the Default content setBuilt before the EPX_CUSTOM set was noticed. A one-field edit per package once the demo is stable.
